glossary.H1B: A US work visa that lets employers hire some workers from abroad for specialized jobs.
glossary.offshoring: Moving work to another country instead of doing it where the company is based.
glossary.asynchronous work: Work people do at different times, rather than needing everyone to be online together.
glossary.equity: Ownership in a company, rather than lending it money.
glossary.Git: A tool for keeping a history of code changes and combining work.
glossary.source control: Tools for keeping track of changes to code and helping developers work on it together.
glossary.agent: An AI system that can take steps and use tools to get a task done, not just answer questions.
glossary.monorepo: One repository that holds code for many projects or services.
glossary.commit: A saved record of changes in a project; this site treats posts like commits.
glossary.DuckDB: A tool for analyzing data on one machine; it can keep working by using the computer’s storage when memory fills up.
glossary.DuckLake: A data format designed to work across different database setups.
glossary.Trino: A tool for asking questions of data stored in a warehouse.
glossary.HogLake: PostHog’s own open format for organizing tables in its warehouse.
glossary.lakehouse: A way to store lots of data while still making it easy to work with like a database.
glossary.catalog: A list of a warehouse’s tables and details about them.
glossary.snapshot: A saved state of a running virtual machine that can be started again later.
glossary.single-node: A setup where one machine does the work, rather than splitting it across several machines.
glossary.query optimizer: The part of a database that picks a way to answer a data question efficiently.
glossary.pgwire: The way Postgres apps communicate with a database over a network.
glossary.TTL: Time to live: how long a saved item or sign-in token stays valid.
glossary.fork: A separate copy of a shared software project that people can take in a different direction.
glossary.public relations: Work aimed at shaping how the public sees a person or group.
glossary.authorised biography: A book about someone written with their permission and cooperation.
glossary.stakeholders: People or groups with an interest in, or affected by, a decision.
glossary.frontier AI: The most capable AI systems being built at a particular time.
glossary.FLOPs: Floating-point operations: a count of computer math steps, used here as a measure of how much compute a run takes.
glossary.export control: A government rule that limits sending certain goods or technology across borders.
